interconnectors.name: Eastern Green Link 1 (Torness to Hawthorn Pit)

ai_summary:
Scotland's power grid is currently demonstrating exceptional low-carbon performance alongside persistent transmission bottlenecks. Real-time telemetry indicates wind generation reaching a formidable 4.4 GW, driving Scottish carbon intensity down to an impressive 32 gCO2/kWh. This robust volume underscores the region's critical capacity to displace fossil fuel generation across the wider Great Britain electricity network.

Nevertheless, structural transmission constraints continue to impede total system efficiency. Total wasted energy has reached 217.5 MWh, reflecting acute curtailment events. Despite strong output, cross-border transmission limits—primarily across the B6 Scottish-English boundary—restrict the export of surplus electricity to southern demand centers. Grid operators are consequently forced to intervene through costly balancing mechanism instructions, curtailing zero-marginal-cost wind assets to maintain network stability.

To capture the full value of periods exceeding 4.4 GW of wind generation, accelerated strategic interventions are essential. Expanding high-voltage direct current (HVDC) links, integrating co-located battery storage systems north of the border, and incentivizing flexible industrial demand will be critical. Without these structural upgrades, Scottish generation will continue to achieve stellar environmental benchmarks while incurring avoidable economic friction from energy curtailment.
